newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers to promote grain export to Morocco.
newsitem.headline: French farmers to promote grain export to Morocco.

text.p: French grain producers plan to open a Moroccan office this summer to help promote exports in the face of fierce competition from other world suppliers, particularly the United States, officials from producers' association Cerealiers de France said on Friday.
The Casablanca-based office be operational when the new 1997/98 (July/June) campaign starts, they said.

Exporters, who dealt mainly with Morocco's national grain office before the privatisation of the grain sector, are particularly eager to develop new ties with the flurry of private operators let loose by liberalisation.
"Our objective is to strengthen our position on the Moroccan market in midst of privatisation," one official said.
Morocco is one of the top destinations for French grain but fierce U.S. competition made a dent in that supremacy and exporters fear that liberalisation may worsen the situation.
"We want to be more in touch with our main market. We need to promote our products and assess local needs," one official said.
Latest data from the International Grains Council (IGC) suggested Morocco may import 1.4 million tonnes of wheat and flour in 1996/97 against 2.2 million the previous season.
For the first eight months of of the 1996/97 season France sold 533,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Morocco against 676,359 tonnes in the past campaign.
